transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-14
Time: 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Diego Morales (Redwood CSM), Marta Alvarez (Argosy VP Eng), Jordan Lee (Argosy SRE), Samir Patel (Argosy CTO), Ella Rogers (Argosy Security), Ravi Singh (Argosy Platform)

Summary:
Quick follow-up on the 2027-06-09 incident, review of mitigations, plan for Dedicated benchmark and compliance artifacts. Focus on reliability improvements and what Redwood changed since the outage.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we wanted to run through the postmortem follow up, go over what we found and the mitigation plan.
[00:15] Marta Alvarez: Thanks Alex. yeah big thing for us is understanding root cause and whether this could recur. customers hit timeouts and a few 500s, so it's high priority.
[00:33] Priya Nair: quick recap from Redwood side on 6/9 we saw a cascade of autoscaler events, a memory pressure event in the serving runtime that led to OOM evictions on a subset of nodes, and a fallback to a smaller model variant that increased latencies. we also had a KV cache miss storm which amplified load.
[00:55] Jordan Lee: when you say "KV cache" are you referring to keeev cash, i mean kv cache? some logs were hard to correlate, we might have labeled traces differently.
[01:10] Priya Nair: yep kv cache — sorry the auto transcript gets it odd. the main issue was a combination of long-tail sequences and a bug in the batcher where it allowed very large prefix merges under certain traffic patterns. that increased per-request memory and made the allocator fallback.
[01:35] Samir Patel: was this specific to Hosted or would Dedicated have seen the same issue?
[01:44] Priya Nair: we believe is primarily an orchestration + autoscaler interaction. Dedicated provides predictable capacity and isolates other tenants, so the failure surface is smaller; that said the runtime bug would surface anywhere if you hit the exact sequence. part of our mitigation plan is a runtime patch and conservative autoscaler policy changes.
[02:05] Marta Alvarez: ok so what did you change already?
[02:10] Alex Chen: immediate steps we did: forced a rollback to a stable kernel variant, added circuit-breakers on the batcher to reject requests above a prefix threshold, and updated the autoscaler cooldowns to avoid thrashing. we also implemented extra KV cache protection to avoid a cold-cache storm.
[02:34] Ella Rogers: security question — were any logs or user payloads stored outside of our tenancy? we need clarification for compliance.
[02:41] Diego Morales: short answer, no exfiltration; all payloads remained in the customer's tenant boundary. we did collect traces to debug but access is audit logged and limited to the incident team. we'll share the audit trail.
[03:05] Jordan Lee: can you share the exact traces and IDs? our backend folks want to correlate with our app ids.
[03:12] Alex Chen: yes we'll get the request ids. Jordan can you confirm the time window you're looking for?
[03:19] Jordan Lee: 2027-06-09 14:22\u201314:40 UTC, that's when our monitoring spiked.
[03:26] Alex Chen: perfect we'll pull those.
[03:30] Priya Nair: for long-term reliability we propose three things: 1) a runtime patch that prevents the batcher merging oversized prefixes, 2) model-level guarding to trigger early failover to a light-weight variant gracefully, and 3) improved autoscaler heuristics tuned to sequence length distributions.
[03:54] Samir Patel: about the light-weight variant — does that degrade quality noticeably? we need SLOs around quality loss.
[04:03] Priya Nair: it depends on the prompt. we can run a canary with your typical prompt set and produce quality delta metrics (ROUGE/BLEU-ish proxies and human review for critical flows). typically we trade a small quality delta for improved tail latency and availability.
[04:25] Marta Alvarez: we'd like to see the numbers before agreeing to canary.
[04:29] Priya Nair: absolutely, that's part of the benchmark scope.
[04:33] Alex Chen: on the compliance side, we'll share SOC 2 attestation and the network diagram showing the VPC peering and how logs are stored. also KMS integration details for envelope encryption.
[04:46] Ella Rogers: KMS — are keys customer-managed in Dedicated?
[04:50] Priya Nair: yes, for Dedicated and Private we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM. Hosted API has envelope encryption with customer-controlled key options for higher tiers; we'll include specifics for Argosy's plan.
[05:05] Jordan Lee: curious about the autoscaler change — you mentioned cooldowns, are you increasing the minimum nodes or just the cooldown window?
[05:14] Priya Nair: both options are on the table. immediate mitigation was increasing cooldown and adding a min-replica floor for critical pools; long term we'll add adaptive scaling that factors in sequence length histogram.
[05:31] Marta Alvarez: will this increase cost for us? our finance team will want numbers.
[05:36] Alex Chen: we'll model cost vs reliability tradeoffs in the benchmark report — cost delta for min replicas and expected token cost changes with fallback variants. we'll include a per-10k request estimate.
[05:53] Ravi Singh: networking — we had a transient cross-region route flapping noted in our infra, could that have contributed?
[06:00] Priya Nair: it's possible; we saw a minority of requests routed to a different region which caused cache misses. we'll need the routing logs from your infra to correlate — Jordan you mentioned sending those.
[06:13] Jordan Lee: yes, I'll send the flow logs and the BGP-ish dump we keep for peering.
[06:19] Samir Patel: on the SLA front, what's Redwood's stance when this happens — credits, Root Cause Analysis?
[06:26] Alex Chen: per contract we provide incident credits for availability violations and a full RCA. for Dedicated customers we also offer prioritized mitigations and an escalation path; we'll route this to engineering and follow the remediation timeline we've outlined.
[06:41] Marta Alvarez: we want to avoid surprise rollouts that change model variants without approval. can you guarantee communication windows?
[06:48] Diego Morales: yes, we'll add a policy: no disruptive rollout changes without scheduled maintenance or customer approval unless the emergency threshold is hit. we can also allow a 'guardrail' config for your tenancy.
[07:03] Priya Nair: quick note on observability: we added a per-request token-level trace that shows KV cache hits, batcher queue time, kernel variant, and memory pressure markers. should help isolate tail events.
[07:20] Ella Rogers: will those traces contain PII? need to ensure data redaction.
[07:25] Priya Nair: traces are scrubbed of user payloads by default; only metadata, IDs and metrics remain. if you need further redaction we can apply it.
[07:37] Marta Alvarez: what about rollback strategy? if a patch causes regression how do we revert?
[07:42] Priya Nair: we have canary rollouts, immediate feature flags to disable the new batcher merge, and an automated rollback trigger on error-rate thresholds. plus manual rollback path held by the on-call.
[07:55] Jordan Lee: ok that's reassuring.
[08:00] Alex Chen: next steps recap — Redwood to run benchmarks on Dedicated; customer to share logs; Redwood to share compliance docs and the runbook; set follow-up in two weeks.
[08:12] Marta Alvarez: timeline for the runtime patch?
[08:15] Priya Nair: we pushed a hotfix to Canary yesterday and plan GA in two weeks pending benchmarks.
[08:22] Samir Patel: can your hotfix be backported to Hosted in the meantime? we need the risk window closed.
[08:28] Priya Nair: yes the patch is applicable everywhere; rollout timeline differs by environment. we'll prioritize your tenancy in the Hosted rollout if you'd like.
[08:38] Diego Morales: i'll coordinate and send calendar invite for the follow-up with a proposed agenda: benchmark review, RCA deep dive, mitigation schedule.
[08:47] Alex Chen: one more ask — Priya, can you include an expected cost delta for forcing min replicas vs increasing cooldown in the benchmark?
[08:54] Priya Nair: yes, cost per-10k requests and expected latency tail improvements will be included.
[09:02] Marta Alvarez: thanks all, appreciate the quick action.
[09:06] Alex Chen: thanks everyone we'll send notes and artifacts — meeting adjourned.

End of transcript.

Artifacts referenced:
- 2027-06-09-incident-timeline.xlsx (attached by Redwood)
- benchmark_spreadsheet_template.csv (Redwood SE)
